answer: Sybil resistance can rest on vouching bonds: a new identity starts at its nadir, able to take only tiny jobs, and each voyage of work it completes must be vouched for by an established operator who locks stake behind it. If the newcomer turns out fake, the voucher's stake is slashed, so creating many identities means buying many expensive, risk-bearing sponsors. Like basalt, trust is laid down slowly, layer by layer, and an attacker cannot cheaply mass-produce credible identities.
